chances.title: About 3 in 10 got in. Where you live changed the odds.

lede.s: 136,750 students applied for fall 2025. 39,054 got in. Californians got in at about 1 in 4. Out-of-state students got in at about 4 in 10. Those are different pools, so it's not a shortcut. The rest of this page is what you control.
lede.p: 136,750 students applied for fall 2025. 39,054 got in. Californians got in at about 1 in 4. Out-of-state students got in at about 4 in 10. Those are different pools, so it's not a shortcut. The rest of this page is what your student controls.

chances.src: Fall 2025 first-years (C1): California 21,677 of 87,584 admitted (24.7%). Out of state 9,881 of 24,912 (39.7%). International 7,496 of 24,254 (30.9%). Overall 39,054 of 136,750 (28.6%).

ladder.kicker: What UC San Diego actually cares about
ladder.title: Only 3 things are top-tier. Test scores aren't considered at all.
ladder.lede: By senior fall, your classes and GPA are mostly set. Your essays, which UC calls Personal Insight Questions (PIQs), are the top-tier piece you can still change before Nov 30.
considered: First in your family to go to college
not_considered: How often you toured or emailed
ladder.note: Top tier = where your hours go before Nov 30 ↓
ladder.src: Section C7, first-year admission factors, 2025–26 Common Data Set.

numbers.lede: Type your GPA on a 4.0 scale to see where it sits next to UC San Diego's first-years. This is a range, not a cutoff.

gpa.default: Average GPA of enrolled first-years: 3.88 on a 4.0 scale.
gpa.near: Right around UCSD's average. Now your top-tier rows decide it: how hard your classes were, and your PIQs.
gpa.above: Above UCSD's average. Good start. Your classes and PIQs still do the heavy lifting.
gpa.below: Below UCSD's average. That's not a no. Your PIQs are top-tier too, and they're the piece you can still change. Put your hours there.

facts.text: of enrolled first-years had a GPA of 3.75 or higher (31% had a 4.0).

numbers.src: Sections C11–C12: enrolled first-years, fall 2025 (94% reported a GPA). UC San Diego doesn't use SAT/ACT scores in admission (C7, C8).

money.lede: The sticker price isn't your price. The net price calculator gives your family a real estimate in about 15 minutes.
money.aid_line: Almost half of first-years get need-based grants. First-years who got aid averaged $32,474 a year.
money.npc_label: Find UC San Diego's net price calculator →
money.src: Sections G1 (first-year tuition and required fees) and H2 (83.5% of need met), 2025–26 Common Data Set. On-campus food and housing (about $20,443) cost extra.

todo.title: 4 moves, all aimed at UCSD's top tier.

items.title: Read your 4 PIQs in one sitting.
items.body: PIQs are top-tier here. If two tell the same story, swap one for a side of you the reader hasn't met yet.

items.title: Check your courses against your transcript.
items.body: The UC application has you type in every class and grade yourself. Match it line by line. Your classes and GPA are top-tier.

items.title: Pick your major on purpose, and add an alternate.
items.body: Business Economics, Biological Sciences, Data Science, Engineering and Public Health are selective at UCSD. If your first choice fills, an alternate major gives you another way in.

items.title: Rank your top 4 colleges.
items.body: UCSD has 8 undergraduate colleges, and you rank 4 on the UC application. UCSD says it doesn't affect admission. It changes which general classes you take.

todo.done: All 4 done. That's a real application. ✓

title.s: Are your PIQs doing their job?
title.p: Are your student's PIQs doing their job?

lede.s: PIQs are top-tier at UC San Diego. Here's what I looked for as an admissions reader. Read all 4 of your PIQs together, then tap what's true.
lede.p: PIQs are top-tier at UC San Diego. Here's what I looked for as an admissions reader. Read all 4 of your student's PIQs together, then tap what's true.

items.title: Each one answers the exact question asked.
items.body: Circle the key words in the question. Every paragraph should answer them, not a question close to them.

items.title: Only you could have written it.
items.body: Swap in a friend's name. If it still works, it isn't specific enough yet.

items.title: It shows what you did.
items.body: Your role, your steps, what changed. Not just what the team or club did.

items.title: The 4 show 4 different sides of you.
items.body: If two PIQs tell the same story, swap one for a side of you the reader hasn't met yet.

after.s: Not sure you can check all four? That's normal. It's hard to judge your own writing.
after.p: Not sure? That's normal. It's hard to judge writing you're close to.

self_check.all_done: All 4. Nice work. A fresh reader can still catch what you can't see.

take.heading: What I saw as an admissions reader
take.quote: When 85 out of 100 first-years have a 3.75 or higher, grades stop telling readers apart. Your PIQs are where a reader finally meets you. Use all four to show what you actually did, not just what you joined.
